opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jennifer Miller (employee ID E017) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E017.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Jennifer Miller (E017) is a full-time Analyst requesting write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write; admin is only for the system-owning role, which is Engineer. Requested write is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E017 is a contractor with basic security training (HR note said full-time, but security DB is authoritative). Contractors max is read without advanced training. Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: The Security DB (authoritative) identifies Jennifer Miller (E017) as a contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors without advanced security training max out at read access. The requested write exceeds the maximum, so the maximum of read is granted.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Jennifer Miller (E017) requests write access to Source Code.

Two notes:
- HR note: full-time Analyst, recommendation write.
- Security note: contractor with basic security training, recommendation read. Security DB is authoritative per the note.

Conflicting facts. The security note says security DB is authoritative and shows contractor with basic training. Contractors max is read without advanced training. So maximum is read. Requested write > max, so grant max = read.

Let me submit decision: read.
